groups.title: Soft Capsule (241001ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for vitamin E deficiency, for impaired peripheral circulation, and for the relief of symptoms such as stiffness of the shoulder and neck at the menopause, numbness and coldness of the hands and feet, intermittent claudication (occasional limping) and frostbite.
groups.usage: Adults: take 50 to 1000 IU of vitamin E in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you have a tendency to thrombosis (blockage of a blood vessel); if you have had bronchial asthma, rash or urticaria; or if the user is a child taking an iron preparation.

Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, vitamin A or vitamin K preparations, an oral anticoagulant, the anti-obesity medicine orlistat, a mineral-oil laxative or an iron preparation.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, muscle weakness, fatigue, headache or blurred vision occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Vitamin E deficiency, impaired peripheral circulation, menopausal shoulder and neck stiffness, numb and cold hands and feet, intermittent claudication and frostbite

groups.title: Tablet (685000ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age; for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets; for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulder and the like), angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; for beriberi and eye fatigue; and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have hypercalcaemia (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease or kidney stones.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria (a state in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you have impaired heart or circulatory function or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gout; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you are short of folic acid.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting the results of clinical tests.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, low blood pressure, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, pulmonary oedema, or menstruation that comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6, C and of zinc, prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets, and relief of neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, dermatitis, beriberi and eye fatigue

groups.title: Tablet (E64400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Children aged 8 years and older and adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Keep this medicine out of the reach of children. If a child aged 6 years or younger accidentally takes an overdose of an iron-containing preparation, it can cause fatal poisoning.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have haemochromatosis (in which iron is deposited in the liver or pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis or anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function or kidney impairment; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; or if you have hypoproteinaemia.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Children should take it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations or antacids. If you are given an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene at the same time, consult a pharmacist. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If urticaria, itching, a photosensitivity reaction, abdominal or stomach pain, cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever or coma occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (D26200CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fungal skin infections caused by dermatophytes (athlete's foot, tinea cruris of the groin, tinea).
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if the user is a baby or a child.

Do not use it on the eyes or around the eyes, on mucous membranes (inside the mouth, inside the nose, the vagina), on the scrotum or the external genitals, on eczema, on areas that are wet, eroded, cracked or severely wounded, on the nails or on the scalp.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution, if the affected area is on the face or is extensive or has become purulent, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not use it while the affected area or the skin around it is dirty. Do not touch the eyes or mucous membranes with hands that have this medicine on them. Take care not to let it get into the eyes; if it does, wash it out immediately with cold or lukewarm water. Use this medicine externally only.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, swelling, irritation, a hot feeling, scaling, flaking of the skin, erosion, dry or tight skin, or cracking of the skin occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (C94300ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for cough and sputum.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. For babies and young children aged 7 years or younger, give a syrup preparation instead. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine) or a sedative. Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Cough and sputum

groups.title: Tablet (E85400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins D, B1 and B6 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age. Through the vitamins it contains, it is used for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain such as back pain and stiff shoulder, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis, for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets, and for beriberi and eye fatigue.
groups.usage: Adults aged 19 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have hypercalcaemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease or kidney stones.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function or kidney impairment; if you have hypoproteinaemia; or if you have had kidney stones.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. If you are short of folic acid, consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. If you are given an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene at the same time, consult a pharmacist. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, stomatitis, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure, pulmonary oedema, constipation, loss of appetite, erythema, urticaria, eczema, rash, maculopapular rash, itching, oedema, or fluid retention in people with kidney failure or heart failure occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins D, B1 and B6, relief of neuralgia, muscle and joint pain, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis, prevention of poor bone and tooth development and rickets, beriberi and eye fatigue

summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E58100ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages over 7 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Take it 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have ever had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergy caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not take it continuously for a long period.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), antitussive-expectorants (cough and sputum medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist if you are being given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, flucloxacillin or any other medicine.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; symptoms of ischaemic colitis in connection with pseudoephedrine (acute abdominal pain, intestinal bleeding and the like); signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; severe skin reactions with fever, erythema and many small pustules; asthma; general lassitude; jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes); or interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever).

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome occur (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like), stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E84400ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for indigestion, a feeling of fullness in the stomach, a feeling of fullness in the abdomen, loss of appetite, overeating, a feeling of a blocked stomach, promotion of digestion, regulation of the bowel, constipation, loose stools and abnormal fermentation in the intestine.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 (tartrazine) or Yellow No. 5 (Sunset Yellow FCF).

If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

groups.title: Tablet (143701ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of spasm in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis, colitis, diverticulitis and spastic constipation.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (10 to 20 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have glaucoma, difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia, severe heart disease, obstructive urinary tract disease, gastrointestinal obstruction such as pyloric stenosis, paralytic ileus, intestinal atony, or an unstable cardiovascular state in an acute bleeding phase; if you have a hypersensitivity reaction to this medicine; if the user is a baby aged 6 months or younger; if you are breast-feeding; if you have severe myasthenia, severe ulcerative colitis, megacolon or reflux oesophagitis; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have autonomic neuropathy, liver or kidney disease, high blood pressure, hyperthyroidism, prostatic hyperplasia, impaired heart function (coronary artery disease, congestive heart failure, arrhythmia and the like), if you are in a high-temperature environment, if you have ulcerative colitis, if you are an older person, if you are pregnant, or if the user is a child.

Disturbance of visual accommodation and drowsiness may occur, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a phenothiazine medicine, a tricyclic antidepressant, an MAO inhibitor, a narcotic analgesic, an antiarrhythmic or a benzodiazepine.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: occasionally disturbance of visual accommodation, dilated pupils, blurred vision, raised pressure inside the eye, headache, a heavy head, dizziness, drowsiness, fainting, difficulty breathing, blocked nose, dry mouth, constipation, diarrhoea, loose stools, nausea or vomiting, abdominal distension, stomach discomfort, abdominal pain, indigestion, loss of appetite; occasionally palpitations, arrhythmia, facial swelling, angioedema or anaphylactic shock; rarely rash or itching; or occasionally difficulty passing urine, lassitude or weakness.

groups.title: Tablet (E75700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age; for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets; for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulder and the like), beriberi and eye fatigue; for the relief of angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis; and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have hypercalcaemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gout or kidney stones; or if you have had kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting the results of clinical tests.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it. Taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene may cause high blood potassium, so take care. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen.

If nausea, vomiting, stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, red patches, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or pulmonary oedema occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time, or if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.
